notes:
Diastema 0.31.0-beta.2 (beta)

What you will notice

A few messages now say "the chart" where they used to say "Open Dental", when they are about something in the patient's record: their email address, mobile phone, birthdate, allergies, medicines, language, or whether they may be texted. A few scheduling messages say "location" where they named Open Dental's clinics. The meaning is the same; only those words changed.

Where you will see it:

- Patient forms (the patient's Forms card, the New patient paperwork list, sending and resending forms): "There's no email address in the chart for this patient", "Email bounced: check the email address in the chart", "There's no mobile phone in the chart", the locked-link message ("check the birthdate in the chart"), and the notes after a signed form is filed (for example "The family and guarantor in the chart weren't changed").
- Settings, Patient forms (the form editor): "Prefilled from the chart", "Fill from the chart", "Their medicines from the chart" and "Their allergies from the chart", and the note line's help.
- Procedure forms (the setup sheet): "Alerts from the chart", and "No allergies, premedication or medical note in the chart."
- Treatment plans (Send on the patient page): the messages about a missing email address, mobile phone or birthdate, a bounced email, a locked link, and "The chart says not to text this patient."
- Follow-ups: "To the patient's mobile phone in the chart."
- Card payments (Take payment, Statements, payment plans, receipts): "The chart has no email address for this patient", statements going "to the email in the chart", and the missing-birthdate message for statements.
- Texting (New text, the conversation, Settings, Texts): "The chart says this patient doesn't want texts", "OK to text in the chart", and the Spanish line "Spanish for a patient whose language is Spanish in the chart."
- Online scheduling (Settings, Try it): a chair "in another location", and a day closed for a chair's location.
- Letters: the fill-in "Where the visit is (an office with locations)".

Everything else reads exactly as before. Nothing Diastema writes into the patient's chart changed, and messages and settings you have already saved keep their words.

Also in this beta (first released in 0.29.2, and new to the beta channel)

- Settings, Treatment plans, Procedure descriptions has a third choice: Diastema's everyday term (where it has one). Plans then name each procedure in plain words without changing anything in Open Dental. Where a procedure has no everyday term, its description shows.
- The Layman's terms page can take back terms Diastema added to Open Dental: Remove from Open Dental clears a term only where it is still exactly Diastema's suggestion, checked again just before it is cleared, so a term your office typed itself is never removed.
